Define oxidation/reduction by oxygen, hydrogen, electrons and oxidation state.
keyPoints: ["Oxidation involves electron loss.","Reduction involves electron gain."]
modelAnswer: Oxidation is gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, loss of electrons, or an increase in oxidation state. Reduction is loss of oxygen, gain of hydrogen, gain of electrons, or a decrease in oxidation state. They occur together in a redox reaction.

stem: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen/hydrogen and gain/loss of electrons.
keyPoints: ["Both processes occur simultaneously in redox reactions.","Electron loss is oxidation and electron gain is reduction."]
modelAnswer: In both definitions, oxidation is the gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, loss of electrons, or increase in oxidation state. Reduction is the loss of oxygen, gain of hydrogen, gain of electrons, or decrease in oxidation state. The oxygen and hydrogen definitions describe transfer of atoms, while the electron and oxidation-state definitions describe the underlying charge change.

stem: State any three rules for assigning oxidation numbers to free elements, ions, atoms and molecules.
keyPoints: ["Free elements have oxidation number $0$.","Ion charge determines the oxidation number of a simple ion.","Sums are $0$ in neutral compounds and equal the charge in ions."]
modelAnswer: Three rules are: the oxidation number of a free element is $0$; the oxidation number of a simple ion equals its charge; and the algebraic sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound is $0$. For a polyatomic ion, the sum equals the ion charge.

Identify the oxidizing and reducing agents in H2S + Cl2 → S + 2HCl.
keyPoints: ["The oxidizing agent is reduced.","The reducing agent is oxidized."]
modelAnswer: In $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{S}+2\mathrm{HCl}$, sulfur changes from oxidation state $-2$ in $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ to $0$ in sulfur, so $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ is the reducing agent. Chlorine changes from $0$ in $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ to $-1$ in chloride in $\mathrm{HCl}$, so $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ is the oxidizing agent.

stem: Identify the oxidizing and reducing agents in 2KI + Cl2 → 2KCl + I2.
keyPoints: ["$\\mathrm{KI}$ donates electrons and is oxidized.","$\\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ accepts electrons and is reduced."]
modelAnswer: In $2\mathrm{KI}+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow2\mathrm{KCl}+\mathrm{I}_{2}$, iodide in $\mathrm{KI}$ is oxidized to iodine, so $\mathrm{KI}$ is the reducing agent. Chlorine is reduced to chloride, so $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ is the oxidizing agent.

stem: Identify oxidizing agents in two reactions.
keyPoints: ["An oxidizing agent is reduced.","Identify the reactant containing the element whose oxidation number decreases."]
modelAnswer: The oxidizing agents are the reactants that are reduced. In $2\mathrm{NH}_{3}+3\mathrm{CuO}\rightarrow3\mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{N}_{2}+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{CuO}$ is reduced to copper, so it is an oxidizing agent. In $2\mathrm{FeCl}_{2}+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow2\mathrm{FeCl}_{3}$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ is reduced to chloride, so it is an oxidizing agent.

What is corrosion? Write its chemical reaction. Describe any one method to prevent corrosion.
keyPoints: ["Corrosion involves oxidation and reduction.","Painting blocks oxygen and moisture from reaching the metal."]
modelAnswer: Corrosion is a natural electrochemical process in which a metal reacts with oxygen and moisture in its environment, forming more stable compounds such as oxides. For iron, rusting can be represented generally as iron reacting with oxygen and water to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, $\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}\cdot x\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$. One prevention method is painting: the coating forms a barrier between the metal and its environment.

stem: Explain sacrificial protection and galvanizing as methods of prevention of corrosion.
keyPoints: ["Sacrificial protection uses a more active metal.","Galvanizing applies a zinc coating to iron or steel."]
modelAnswer: Sacrificial protection makes the metal to be protected the cathode and connects it to a more active metal, such as magnesium, which corrodes in its place. Galvanizing coats clean iron or steel with zinc; the zinc layer acts as a protective barrier and can also provide sacrificial protection if the surface is scratched.
